ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against FATF/AMF PEP definitions, UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists (Framework Regulations 765/2006 and 269/2014), OFAC SDN List, and French domestic DGDDI/DGCCRF screening directives; enhanced due diligence triggered by PEP status or high-risk third-country exposure per EU Delegated Regulation 2016/1675.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Infogreffe / INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) National Register
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be exclusively in French or using standard Latin characters; French law requires no specific legal suffix for SARL formation but the chosen name must be available in the RNCS (Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés) and not misleading as to the corporate form
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying public or institutional authority (e.g., 'République', 'Ministère', 'Banque de France')
Words reserved for regulated activities (e.g., 'Banque', 'Assurance', 'Avocat') without ministerial or supervisory authorization
Misleading references to a public limited company (e.g., 'ANONYME' or 'COMMANDITE') for an SARL structure
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon formal rejection by the INPI/Registrar, the founders may submit a written administrative appeal to the INPI Director within 30 calendar days of notification; additionally, judicial recourse before the Commercial Court (Tribunal de commerce) is available under Article L.123-4 of the French Commercial Code for unreasonable rejection, with a 2-month statutory limitation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted solely via regulated domiciliation companies (société de domiciliation) under French Law (Law No. 96-987 and Ordinance 2000-916); the domiciliation contract must enable receipt of legal process and allow physical inspection; foreign virtual-office-only arrangements without a physical French presence do not satisfy statutory substance requirements for an SARL.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for B2B MRO e-commerce Operations (standard remote sales profile risks <5% annual likelihood); however, unannounced inspection risk increases if tax irregularities are flagged, requiring the registered office or domiciliation provider to maintain full administrative substance and accessibility.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce, articles L. 223-1 et seq. and L. 225-1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of the Tribunal de Commerce
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de la société (Articles of Association)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital of 1 EUR; no escrow account required for SARL
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders of the proposed Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) hereby resolve as follows: 1. The Company is incorporated with a share capital of one thousand euros (EUR 1,000), fully subscribed and paid up by the initial shareholders as per the attached share subscription agreement. 2. The registered office is adopted at [full French address], and the gérants are appointed as follows: [Name] as gérant unique with unlimited powers, and [Name] as gérant. 3. The Articles of Association are adopted in the form provided, authorizing the gérants to file the incorporation documents with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, publish the legal notices, and perform all acts necessary for the proper formation and operation of the Company. This resolution is adopted unanimously by the shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, Sign, Notarize Articles of Association and File for Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet-Entreprises.fr online portal or direct submission to RCS of the Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: 1. Prepare the Articles of Association in French. 2. Obtain signatures from all shareholders. 3. Have the documents notarized by a French notary. 4. Submit the notarized statuts via the guichet-entreprises.fr portal or by mail to the RCS. 5. Pay the filing fees and obtain the SIREN number. 6. Publish the creation notice in a legal gazette.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the applicant may submit amendments or additional documents within the prescribed period to cure the deficiency.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique et de la Cohésion des territoires
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharges or emissions applicable to wholesale distribution activities

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural safety inspections for the registered office; obtain occupational health and safety clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Paris; portal: impots.gouv.fr; entity registration via the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and INSEE.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL is incorporated through the Guichet Unique, which transmits the dossier to the RCS and INSEE; after delivery of SIREN and SIRET numbers, the DGFiP automatically assigns the intra-community VAT identification number (format: FR + two-digit key + SIREN) under Article 286 ter of the French General Tax Code (CGI). A foreign entity not established in France must apply for a simplified VAT registration using Form 1546 (immatriculation simplifiée) filed with the DGFiP before its first taxable French supply, or register under the Non-Union OSS, Union OSS, or Import One-Stop Shop (IOSS) regime for distance and B2C service supplies. A foreign entity establishing a permanent establishment in France must file Form P0(C4) with the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises and obtain a full French VAT identification number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The SARL is subject by default to French corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) at the standard rate of 25%, unless the company validly elects for the income-tax regime under Article 239 bis AA CGI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Election for partnership-style income taxation (Impôt sur le Revenu, IR) under Article 239 bis AA CGI for eligible closely-held or family SARLs meeting statutory conditions (employee headcount, turnover and balance-sheet ceilings, shareholder composition, and absence of commercial rental activity); option for the IR regime of a SARL de famille; election for fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) for a SARL at least 95% held by a French tax-integrated parent under Article 223 A CGI; hybrid mismatch alignments under the transposition of ATAD 1 and ATAD 2 (Articles 212 bis and 209-0 B CGI) deny deductions in respect of hybrid entity and hybrid transfer mismatches and treat the French SARL as an opaque entity under domestic law; the IR/IS election operates as the functional French equivalent of a check-the-box classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (French Value Added Tax).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: A domestic-established SARL is subject to compulsory VAT registration from the date of incorporation, with no minimum turnover threshold; however, an eligible small French-established business may elect for the franchise en base de TVA only where annual taxable turnover remains below €91,900 (principal supplies of goods and hospitality/food services) or €37,500 (provision of services), in which case it may not deduct input VAT. For foreign suppliers: a non-established supplier of B2C services must register in France from its first euro of taxable sales (Non-Union OSS); imported distance-sold goods are covered by IOSS where consignment value does not exceed €150; an EU-established supplier making intra-EU distance sales must register under Union OSS when annual cross-border distance sales exceed the €10,000 Union threshold. The SARL's B2B MRO catalogue supplies to French customers are taxable at the 20% standard rate from the first euro.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is deploying a mandatory B2B e-invoicing and B2C e-reporting framework under the 2024 Finance Law and CGI Article 289 bis. Mandatory issuance and receipt of structured electronic invoices applies to large enterprises and mid-sized enterprises (ETI) from 1 September 2026, and to all VAT-taxable persons, including SMEs and micro-enterprises, from 1 September 2027. E-invoices must be exchanged through a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) or the free Portail Public de Facturation (PPF); accepted structured formats are Factur-X (recommended hybrid UN/CEFACT and UBL semantics), UBL 2.1 and CII 16B. B2C transaction data and cross-border supply data are transmitted to the DGFiP through the e-reporting regime. The 2018 anti-fraud cash-register law separately requires certified, tamper-proof POS software (NF 525 or equivalent) for over-the-counter retail sales; France does not operate an Italian-style real-time fiscal clearance stamp, but the DGFiP conducts risk-based electronic audits and may access transaction-level e-reporting data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods outside the European Union are VAT-exempt with credit for input tax (zero-rating) under Article 262-I-1° CGI where the goods are dispatched or transported by the seller, or on the seller's behalf, to a destination outside the EU. Intra-community supplies of goods to a customer identified for VAT in another Member State are exempt under Article 262-0 CGI, subject to retention of the customer's valid EU VAT number and filing of the EC Sales List (état récapitulatif de TVA / DEB). Export-related transport and ancillary services are zero-rated under Article 262-I-2° CGI where they are directly linked to physically exported goods. The SARL's B2B MRO export sales to non-EU industrial clients qualify for zero-rating where the SARL is named as exporter on the customs declaration and the goods physically depart the EU; intra-EU dispatches to VAT-registered industrial resellers and end-users are zero-rated with DEB reporting. Substantiation must be complete within the statutory documentary window to preserve the 0% benefit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Document Administratif Unique / DAU or electronic DELTA-X and ECS export declaration) naming the SARL as exporter and evidencing exit from EU customs territory
Transport documentation proving physical export: Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB), CMR road consignment note, or combined transport document (DCT)
Commercial invoice, packing list, export sales contract and INCOTERM (EXW, FOB, CIF, etc.)
Intra-EU evidence: customer's valid EU VAT number, EC Sales List (DEB) filing confirmation, and transport proof such as CMR
Inward Remittance Certificate (relevé de domiciliation bancaire) or SWIFT MT103/MT950 wire confirmation linking the export customer's payment to the corresponding export invoice
For export-linked services: customs transport declaration and the underlying export contract demonstrating a direct link to the exported physical goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where the SARL cannot demonstrate the physical export or the customer's valid intra-EU VAT status, the DGFiP re-characterises the supply as taxable French VAT at 20% and applies late-payment interest (0.20% per month) plus penalties under Article 1728 CGI: 40% for deliberate under-declaration (manquement délibéré) or 80% for concealment of taxable operations (transaction dissimulée) under Article 1788 A CGI, rising to 100% for fraudulent manoeuvres. Retrospective clawback of output VAT, denial of input VAT recovery, and joint and several liability are asserted in carousel or missing-trader fraud chains; criminal prosecution under Article 1741 CGI may lead to five years' imprisonment and a fine of up to €500,000, aggravated under Article 1743 CGI for habituality or organised fraud. The French administration audits zero-ratings with enhanced risk-scoring, targeting fabricated export documentation and circular goods flows.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) is the central bank and the competent monetary and balance-of-payments statistician; exchange-control supervision is carried out under the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique (French Treasury), while prudential control of credit institutions and payment institutions is exercised by the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution), and financial intelligence/AML enforcement is coordinated through Tracfin.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in France; capital movements, current payments and profit remittances are protected by Articles 63 and 65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and by the French Monetary and Financial Code. No exchange authorization, usance requirement, or import licensing is applicable to ordinary B2B MRO supplies. Dividends and proceeds from a SARL may be remitted to foreign shareholders freely, but the French paying company must apply the relevant withholding tax (generally 25% under Article 119 bis CGI or treaty-reduced/zero rate), verify the economic substance of treaty claimants, and file the withholding return and beneficiary statement. Interest paid to non-resident shareholders is deductible only if Article 212 CGI thin-capitalisation, arm's length and market-rate conditions are met. The only practical restriction is documentary: banks and payment providers will request KYC, source-of-funds, beneficial-ownership and trade-backup evidence before releasing outbound dividends or loan repayments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no statutory obligation to surrender export proceeds, no mandatory conversion of export receivables into EUR, and no time limit for repatriating revenues earned by a French SARL. Export receipts may remain in foreign currency at the company's treasury risk. For Banque de France external-statistics purposes, the bank executing the settlement reports the transaction's country, sector and category from the payment field; exporters should therefore maintain invoices, customs declarations, proof of transport and bank statements for each shipment. No surrender certificate, Central Bank pricing confirmation, or prior license is required for standard MRO hardware export receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank (CACIB) / LCL

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: For a low-risk, non-licensed SARL in MRO e-commerce, a regulated EU fintech or Electronic Money Institution (EMI) is MEDIUM viable for operational and controlled disbursement accounts, but LOW viable as the exclusive treasury rail for capital escrow, substantial cross-border settlements and letters of credit. An EMI passporting into France under the E-Money Directive 2009/110/EC and PSD2 (Directive (EU) 2015/2366) may open segregated client accounts, issue IBANs, process SEPA/Instant and SWIFT payments, and supply inexpensive online banking. The decisive legal constraints are: (i) an EMI is not a credit institution and therefore does not offer protected bank deposits through the French Fonds de Garantie des Dépôts et de Résolution; (ii) not all EMIs support documentary credits, MT103 with full correspondent code or high-value USD clearing; (iii) the French registry/notarial form for the company's capital deposit normally requires a deposit with a bank (établissement de crédit) or a notary rather than an EMI; and (iv) Tracfin reporting and frozen-asset rules still apply, so an EMI cannot reduce the underlying KYC burden.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under CMF Article L.561-5, the credit institution must identify and verify the SARL and its beneficial owners before entering into a banking relationship. For a newly incorporated SARL with non-resident shareholders, a physical presence at a branch or an ACPR-approved secure video-identification interview is generally required for the gérant (manager) and each 25%+ UBO; the bank may also require physical attendance for any individual authorized to open accounts or execute high-value wires. Remote opening is possible under the French decree on electronic identification where the bank uses a verified video endpoint, but acceptance is discretionary and usually limited to natural-person clients rather than complex corporate structures. The practical mandatory file includes a recent Kbis extract, articles of association, identity papers, proof of residence, beneficial-ownership declaration and a board resolution describing the signatory powers; French-language versions or certified translations must be supplied where originals are non-French.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly registered SARL with no historical financials and a single shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised articles of association, up-to-date Kbis, signed shareholder register, capital-subscription certificate, bank's blocked-account certificate (if used), business plan covering ISIC 4791/NAICS 423840 MRO catalogue sales, evidence of warehouse or e-commerce platform, and source-of-funds statements for the paid-up capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate shareholder or UBO in a tax-haven or high-risk FATF jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificate of incorporation/existence, certificate of good standing, group structure chart identifying all UBOs, audited financial statements or company confirmation, certified ID and proof of residential address for individuals, and a reasoned commercial-purpose paper explaining the French market-entry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound capital injection disproportionate to business scale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder source-of-wealth report (12 months bank statements, tax returns, prior dividends, sale escrow agreements), signed loan or capital-increase resolution, funds transfer origin confirmation, confirmation that no funds are derived from third parties without legal documentation, and an independent accounting/legal confirmation of lawful origin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: MRO trade description mismatches between invoices, customs declarations, and bank payment narratives
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Purchase orders, supplier proforma and commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading or airway bills, customs Import/Export declarations (DAU/ENS), Incoterms clause, and a product catalogue identifying the HS codes within ISIC 4791 and NAICS 423840; payment narratives must constantly state 'spare parts / industrial MRO hardware' rather than generic 'goods'.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dividend or interest remittance to a foreign shareholder triggering treaty-reduced withholding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: DTA residence certificate, Form 5000/5051 (depending on treaty), full ownership and holding-period evidence under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where applicable, Article 119 bis analysis, board minutes approving the distribution, and a confirmation that the recipient is the beneficial owner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital from a foreign shareholder must be routed by SWIFT MT103 in EUR (or USD converted by the bank) to the SARL's French IBAN. The sending bank should use a transparent trade/capital narrative in Field 70 within the 140-character limit, e.g. 'CAPITAL INCREASE / AUGMENTATION DE CAPITAL - SARL [company] - SIREN [number] - shareholder resolution [date]', and the receiving French bank will map the transaction to the Banque de France balance-of-payments category for direct investment/capital increase. No French Central Bank prior approval is required, but the bank may require a 'capital/equity injection compliance pack' comprising the notarized resolution, subscribed capital attestation, the shareholders' source-of-funds evidence, and a signed depository instruction for blocked release. For a loan instead of equity, the funds must be booked under a 'compte courant d'associé' agreement with an interest rate calculated on an arm's length basis, registered in the annual accounts and, if significant, disclosed to the bank for the balance-of-payments statistics.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The recommended clearing hierarchy for MRO trade settlements is: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant for Euro-denominated payments to EEA suppliers; (2) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border EUR, USD, GBP or exotic-currency wires, always with invoice and contract reference numbers in Fields 70/72; (3) a documentary Letter of Credit opened or transferred by SWIFT MT700/MT707 under UCP600 for high-value or Asian/overseas suppliers, with first benefiting bank being a Tier-1 French bank; (4) standby letters of credit (MT760) for large distribution contracts; and (5) corporate purchase cards/credit cards for low-ticket e-catalogue purchases, subject to supplier category restrictions. The French SARL should maintain an approved-settlement matrix: wire under EUR [threshold] on trade documents, LC above threshold, and card only for predefined vendors. Payments to counterparties in embargoed/sanctioned countries require screening and Tracfin declarations; the MRO plan should exclude dual-use and military goods as those are subject to export authorisation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX purchases of USD or other trade currencies against EUR for immediate settlement of import invoices
Outright EUR/USD and EUR/third-currency forwards (forward exchange contracts) covering firm MRO purchase or sales commitments, limited to the underlying contract amount and tenor
FX swaps (swap de change) for simultaneous EUR/USD funding in two legs where the treasury needs to bridge value dates of inbound and outbound payments
Cross-currency swaps (usually under ISDA or a French law master agreement) only for larger trade-finance or capital-structure hedging, not for speculative repricing
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where the settlement currency is non-convertible or has no active onshore forward market, back-to-back with the physical supply contract

Vanilla foreign-exchange options (calls/puts) if purchased under a board-approved treasury policy to hedge transactional exposure; sale of uncovered options is not recommended as permissible structural hedging

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting approving annual accounts and deciding on profit appropriation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No authority filing; minutes retained in the company's statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the fiscal year-end under Article L.223-27 of the French Commercial Code
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Any interested party may request court appointment of a liquidator or judicial dissolution; directors may face civil liability for delay-caused losses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit to the commercial registry (dépôt des comptes annuels), including balance sheet, profit and loss statement, notes and shareholders' approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the Guichet Unique operated by INPI/RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of shareholder approval and no later than 7 months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of up to EUR 7,500 for a legal entity; court-ordered coercive fines and eventual RCS strike-off for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale No. 2065 and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE), Direction Générale des Finances Publiques
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal years ending on 31 December: the second working day after 1 May of the following year; for other fiscal year-ends: within 3 months of the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-payment interest of 0.20% plus an uplift of 10% to 80% depending on delay and intent; enforced collection against assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner register update (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) to the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés via Greffe/Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual recurring filing; event-driven update within 30 days of any transfer of SARL shares or other change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 15,000 for legal entities; court-ordered suspension of voting rights and dividend payments until regularisation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local economic contribution (CFE) declaration and payment, where applicable to the commercial establishment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Service des Impôts des Entreprises / local DGFiP collection office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual tax generally payable by 15 December of the tax year; any change in establishment or operating basis must be declared with the annual tax return cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment penalties of 10% plus enforced collection, and loss of any applicable exemptions or reductions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory appointment of a registered auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory when, at the end of a fiscal year, at least two of the three thresholds are exceeded in two consecutive years: total balance sheet over EUR 4,000,000; net turnover over EUR 8,000,000; average staff over 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP per Règlement ANC No. 2014-03 (Plan Comptable Général), incorporating the accounting provisions of Articles L.123-12 through L.123-23 of the French Commercial Code; IFRS applies only to consolidated financial statements of listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a standalone annual UBO re-filing. The RCS beneficial-ownership declaration is event-driven and must be updated within 30 days of any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership. At each annual ordinary general meeting, the company must verify the register of members and rectify the RCS beneficial-ownership declaration for any unreported transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Registre des décisions et documents relatifs à la gérance)
Minute Book (Registre des procès-verbaux des assemblées)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - 15,000 equivalent per year depending on turnover, inventory and group structure
